record.title: ACLArena reports task forgetting in sequential agent training and tests routed LoRA experts
record.summary: An arXiv preprint introduces ACLArena, a controlled study of capability retention across multi-stage agent post-training. On Qwen3-8B-Base, the authors report that sequential math, search, e-commerce and instruction-following stages can overwrite earlier capabilities: after e-commerce training, AIME26 fell from 23.33 to 6.04 and Natural Questions from 45.2 to 14.6. They compare multi-teacher on-policy distillation, replay-based supervised fine-tuning and model merging, then propose Mixture of Low-Rank Experts (MLE), which combines replay-trained shared behavior with separate RL-trained LoRA experts routed by environment context. Reported results approach task-specific experts on several tasks, but the fixed curriculum, single model family and observable-context routing leave transfer and deployment costs unresolved.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: The authors report that sequential post-training of Qwen3-8B-Base across math, search, e-commerce and instruction following produced substantial task-dependent forgetting: after e-commerce training, AIME26 fell from 23.33 to 6.04 and Natural Questions from 45.2 to 14.6; the final checkpoint only partly recovered prior task peaks. Baseline sequential results are reported over three independent runs.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: The paper proposes Mixture of Low-Rank Experts (MLE): replay-filtered supervised fine-tuning over specialist trajectories followed by separate RL-trained LoRA experts routed by observable environment context. In the paper’s Qwen3-8B-Base setup, MLE reports stronger combined in-domain and out-of-domain scores than the shared-checkpoint MMOPD, SDFT and model-merging alternatives on several evaluated tasks; it does not dominate every task-specific expert.

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED_LIMITATION
claims.text: The paper says the experiments mainly use Qwen3-8B-Base and a fixed four-stage curriculum; expert routing under ambiguous or changing environment context and within-episode combinations is untested.

evidence_gaps.description: No independent reproduction or public artifact was inspected for the sequential forgetting analysis or MLE comparisons.
The study uses one fixed four-stage order and one base model family; generalization across model families and curricula is unknown.

MLE routing assumes observable environment/tool context; ambiguous context, context changes and combined specializations within one episode were not tested, and inference latency/memory tradeoffs remain unmeasured.

brief.importance_rationale: If replicated, the paper’s controlled comparison could change how teams design multi-stage agent post-training by showing that sequentially accumulated skills can be overwritten and that task-specific low-rank residuals may retain incompatible specializations. The evidence is a single Qwen3-8B-Base family under a fixed four-stage curriculum, so broader transfer and deployment costs remain unknown.
limitations: The results are author-reported and were not independently reproduced in this review.
The experiments mainly use Qwen3-8B-Base and one fixed four-stage curriculum; transfer across model families, tasks and stage orders is unestablished.
The reported sequential forgetting patterns are task-dependent; consolidation approaches recover different capabilities and introduce tradeoffs rather than uniformly improving all domains.
MLE routes based on observable environment context; ambiguous or changing contexts and combining specializations within one episode remain untested.
The public paper reports benchmark outcomes, not a production deployment; adapter memory, routing latency and serving economics are not established.
brief.summary: An arXiv preprint introduces ACLArena, a controlled study of capability retention across multi-stage agent post-training. On Qwen3-8B-Base, the authors report that sequential math, search, e-commerce and instruction-following stages can overwrite earlier capabilities: after e-commerce training, AIME26 fell from 23.33 to 6.04 and Natural Questions from 45.2 to 14.6. They compare multi-teacher on-policy distillation, replay-based supervised fine-tuning and model merging, then propose Mixture of Low-Rank Experts (MLE), which combines replay-trained shared behavior with separate RL-trained LoRA experts routed by environment context. Reported results approach task-specific experts on several tasks, but the fixed curriculum, single model family and observable-context routing leave transfer and deployment costs unresolved.

technical.claimed_result: The authors report substantial task-dependent forgetting under sequential post-training and propose that a shared replay-trained backbone plus isolated RL-trained LoRA experts can recover a broader set of capabilities than shared-checkpoint consolidation methods in their tested Qwen3-8B-Base setting.
technical.compute_or_cost: The paper uses two NVIDIA H200 nodes for experiments. It does not establish production serving costs, routing latency or adapter memory at deployment.
technical.demonstrated_result: The arXiv paper describes the ACLArena setup, methods and author-reported tables. the research desk did not reproduce the training runs or benchmark results.
technical.implementation_status: Research framework and experimental method described in the preprint; no independent reproduction or production deployment was inspected.
technical.mechanism: MLE first applies replay-based SFT to specialist trajectories to form a shared backbone, freezes that backbone, and trains one low-rank LoRA expert per stage using RL. At inference, it chooses an expert from the observable interaction environment/tool context.
technical.novelty: Provides a controlled comparison of sequential training, multi-teacher on-policy distillation, replay-based self-distillation and parameter merging, then tests parameter-isolated RL LoRA experts as a way to retain interfering task specializations.
technical.regime: Qwen3-8B-Base; fixed curriculum of math, search, e-commerce and instruction following; in-domain and out-of-domain evaluations across reasoning, search, tool-using commerce and instruction following.
technical.reproducibility: The paper provides task and training details, but this review did not inspect a public implementation or checkpoints and did not independently reproduce results.
technical.strongest_baseline: The final sequential Qwen3-8B-Base checkpoint and the paper’s matched MMOPD, SDFT and model-merging alternatives, with independently trained per-task experts as specialization references.

brief.title: ACLArena reports task forgetting in sequential agent training and tests routed LoRA experts
brief.why_it_matters: If replicated across models and curricula, this work could shift multi-stage agent training from assuming capabilities accumulate to explicitly measuring and protecting skills that later stages can overwrite. Its key design tradeoff is retaining task-specific adapters with context-based routing; the evidence does not yet establish transfer, robust routing or deployment cost.
